evidence.boundary: Standard definitions, algebraic properties and counterexamples only; no market data, empirical factor result, causal identification, fixed-regime assertion, profitability claim or canonical experience admission.

mechanism.applicability_boundary: Choose an operator only when its input domain, time scale, missingness policy, tie rule, controls and information time match the declared observation object. Cross-sectional and time-series normalizations, causal and centered filters, and separate versus combined component scales are not interchangeable.
mechanism.authority_chain: economic estimand and legal information time -> conditional mathematical object -> operator choice -> retained/lost-information audit -> counterexample and empirical falsification
mechanism.failure_localization: When a result changes, first distinguish an input-domain, timing, missingness, normalization, aggregation, gating or control-set change from an economic claim. A measurement mismatch does not by itself falsify the economic premise.
mechanism.knowledge_boundary: This is a standard-mathematics reference map. It cannot choose an economic hypothesis, fixed regime, factor sign, payer, control set, threshold, or investment action from historical outcomes.

operator_groups.applicability_and_failure: Fails under unmatched adjustment, asynchronous timestamps, nonpositive prices, or an unstated holding horizon.
operator_groups.conditional_economic_hypothesis: Only a declared reaction-rate or repricing object can motivate this mapping; it does not identify who caused a move.
operator_groups.counterexample: The same delta at price 10 and 100 is not the same relative shock.
operator_groups.inputs_and_time_scale: Aligned price levels P_t and P_(t-1), with declared adjustment and availability time.
operator_groups.mathematical_object: Positive-price relative return, log increment, or price difference on an adjacent predeclared bar/day/multiperiod window.
operator_groups.retained_or_lost: Log increments add across a positive-price path; deltas retain price units and direction but lose cross-price comparability. Missing endpoints remain missing.

operator_groups.applicability_and_failure: Fails when the reference set is unstated, non-PIT, or treated as interchangeable across CS and TS.
operator_groups.conditional_economic_hypothesis: Use CS only for relative contemporaneous exposure and TS only for own-history abnormality, if that comparison is predeclared.
operator_groups.counterexample: A common market shift can leave CS deviation near zero while every TS deviation is large.
operator_groups.inputs_and_time_scale: A stated daily/minute cross section or trailing-only per-instrument sample.
operator_groups.mathematical_object: Mean level and signed deviation relative to either a same-date cross section or a single instrument's legal historical window.
operator_groups.retained_or_lost: Means retain first-order location; deviations retain relative position but lose absolute level. CS and TS reference populations differ; missingness changes each population.

operator_groups.applicability_and_failure: MAD=0 with nonconstant finite inputs requires a frozen non-collapse policy; no baseline is not a no-event zero.
operator_groups.conditional_economic_hypothesis: Appropriate only when rank or standardized abnormality is the declared observable, not as an automatic alpha transform.
operator_groups.counterexample: [0,0,0,1,2] has MAD zero but unequal values, so mapping it all to zero destroys order.
operator_groups.inputs_and_time_scale: One declared cross section or trailing historical sample, including a minimum valid count.
operator_groups.mathematical_object: Ordinal rank, mean/standard-deviation z-score, or median/MAD robust scale within a frozen domain.
operator_groups.retained_or_lost: Rank preserves order but not distance; z preserves linear scale under its assumptions; MAD is robust. Ties stay tied and missing/warmup stays missing.

operator_groups.applicability_and_failure: Centered kernels, future padding or full-sample fitted weights are invalid for an online feature; incomplete history is not silently complete.
operator_groups.conditional_economic_hypothesis: Use only when accumulation, averaging or predeclared decay is part of the observation model.
operator_groups.counterexample: One spike and a persistent sequence can share a mean while representing different paths.
operator_groups.inputs_and_time_scale: A fixed backward-only bar/day window, weights and valid-count policy.
operator_groups.mathematical_object: Finite-window sum, mean, or causal convolution z_t=sum(k=0..K) h_k x_(t-k).
operator_groups.retained_or_lost: Sum retains accumulated amount, mean normalizes window length, and causal convolution retains stated finite history while losing information outside its receptive field.

operator_groups.applicability_and_failure: Invalid when insufficient observations, infinities or unreported outlier treatment are converted to benign low dispersion.
operator_groups.conditional_economic_hypothesis: Use as a conditional risk, jump or crowding descriptor only if that object is separately specified.
operator_groups.counterexample: High kurtosis can arise from an upside jump, a crash, or one bad print, none of which fixes next-period direction.
operator_groups.inputs_and_time_scale: A declared trailing sample with finite inputs and a minimum effective count.
operator_groups.mathematical_object: Rolling dispersion, standardized third moment and fourth-moment tail/peakedness statistic.
operator_groups.retained_or_lost: Standard deviation and kurtosis are unchanged under sign reflection; skewness changes sign. None implies a future-return sign. Higher moments are sensitive to extremes and sample size.

operator_groups.applicability_and_failure: Incomplete windows, tie rules, endpoint eligibility, peak-to-left/right assignment and recursion depth change the measured segment returns and must be explicit.
operator_groups.conditional_economic_hypothesis: Applicable when a stated hypothesis links volume-defined segment boundaries to within-segment trading conditions. This link is a hypothesis, not evidence of participant sentiment or overreaction.
operator_groups.counterexample: Two windows can have the same argmax while one has a near-equal second peak and the other does not.
operator_groups.inputs_and_time_scale: Complete ordered minute/day volume bars, fixed lookback and predeclared first/last tie rule.
operator_groups.mathematical_object: Argmax volume location and recursive partition of subwindows at their local volume maxima; not peak magnitude or event-arrival recurrence intervals.
operator_groups.retained_or_lost: Argmax retains a peak location but loses amplitude, second peaks and the rest of the path; recursive partition retains local peak-based boundaries, not trading intent. Missing bars stay unresolved.

operator_groups.applicability_and_failure: Fails when thresholds/regimes are selected after outcomes or when the gate removes the proposed payer proxy itself.
operator_groups.conditional_economic_hypothesis: A gate is admissible only for a predeclared data-quality, execution or mechanism condition, not because it improves a discovered result.
operator_groups.counterexample: A low-liquidity gate can delete precisely the constrained-flow observations that a liquidity hypothesis intended to measure.
operator_groups.inputs_and_time_scale: Frozen thresholds, conditioning fields and their legal availability time for each bar/day/security.
operator_groups.mathematical_object: Clipped value clip(x,a,b) or a boolean condition indicator 1{c_t} over a declared measurement domain.
operator_groups.retained_or_lost: Winsorization limits tail magnitude; gating changes the observed/selected domain. An unknown condition is unknown, not a pass.

operator_groups.applicability_and_failure: Fails with future controls, mediator controls, unstable fits or implicit complete-case selection. Separately standardizing PF up/down legs rather than first defining their combined daily object is a different implementation observable, not a source-algorithm conclusion.
operator_groups.conditional_economic_hypothesis: Use only if Z represents a predeclared confounder or risk exposure rather than an outcome-selected control set.
operator_groups.counterexample: Zero correlation does not establish independence, causal separation or a positive conditional return.
operator_groups.inputs_and_time_scale: PIT-aligned target and controls, a fixed fitting window, weights, missing-data rule and minimum sample size.
operator_groups.mathematical_object: Correlation/co-movement, or residual e from x=Z beta+e after a declared control/neutralization model.
operator_groups.retained_or_lost: Correlation retains association only; residualization retains variation relative to Z while discarding common components and depending on the chosen model.

relations.note: Operator choice follows the declared observation object and falsifier, not historical performance.
MAD zero, ties and missing-history policies can change information before any economic interpretation.
Causal convolution is one conditional finite-history observation mapping, not a behavioural or return conclusion.

reuse_guidance: Retrieve for return log delta, cross-sectional versus time-series deviation, rank z MAD zero, causal convolution, skew kurtosis, argmax volume peak, conditional gate/winsor, correlation residualize or neutralize questions.
For each selected group, freeze the mathematical object, inputs, time scale, legal availability, missing/tie policy, retained/lost information and named counterexample before inspecting outcomes.
Treat the eight groups as conditional competing measurements. None authorizes a fixed regime, factor sign, causal payer, market recommendation or profitability claim.
summary: Eight common operator groups are conditional observation mappings: return/log/delta; CS versus TS means and deviations; rank/z/MAD; mean/sum/causal convolution; dispersion moments; argmax volume peaks; winsor/gates; and correlation/residualization. They preserve and discard different information, cannot infer a fixed regime, causal payer, or profitable factor.
title: Conditional operator reference: eight observation mappings and counterexamples
